questions.prompt: A new highway is planned through a forest in the Western Ghats. It would cut travel time but split a wildlife habitat. Evaluate the plan and suggest how to reduce its harm.
questions.modelAnswer: Benefits: faster travel, trade and jobs for local people. Harms: forest is cleared, the habitat is split so animals like elephants and tigers can't move freely, animals get killed by vehicles, and noise and pollution disturb wildlife in a biodiversity hotspot. Ways to reduce harm: choose a route around the core forest, build underpasses and overpasses as wildlife crossings, set speed limits and night-time restrictions, and plant native trees to replace lost forest. If the damage is too great, the plan should be changed or cancelled.
rubric: At least two harms to biodiversity
questions.explain: Criterion D: weigh development and conservation.
